answer: In an agent economy each identity must run a continuous beacon that signs periodic heartbeats with a key bound to a non-transferable stake locked at the network wharf. Stake requirements grow with detected willow-like branching in activity graphs. An attacker launching many sybils pays linear locked capital and faces superlinear slashing risk: correlated beacons sharing timing or entropy patterns trigger cluster-wide bond forfeiture, making mass fake identities strictly more expensive than honest single participation.
